# System 573 RTL ↔ Hardware-Witness Audit

## 1. Summary

**14 of 15 candidates confirmed real** (1 refuted: WDOG-01; DIO-03 was also refuted during candidate triage). Of the 14 confirmed, **1 is high-severity (FLASH-001)**, **1 is medium (SECCART-01)**, and **12 are low**. **One-line verdict: the flash bank-decode bug (FLASH-001) is the single most likely root cause of both the self-test stall and any downstream graphics garble; everything else is latent/benign for the current hyperbbc target.** No discrepancy requires hardware to *confirm* — all are decidable by code-reading + the BIOS binary + MAME, which runs our exact data.

## 2. Top suspects for the two open bugs

### (a) Self-test stall (green-0s) — ROOT CAUSE: FLASH-001

| | |
|---|---|
| **Subsystem** | Flash + bank-switch (0x1f500000 control / 4 MB window at 0x1f000000) |
| **Our file:line** | `rtl/s573_flash.v:101-102` — `wire internal = (bank[3:0]==4'b0000);` and `wire [1:0] bank_idx = bank[5:4];` |
| **What's wrong** | The internal-flash bank index is decoded from `bank[5:4]` (and gated on `bank[3:0]==0`), so only control-register values `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30` select onboard banks. But the runtime BIOS writes the bank number in the **low** bits (`0x00/0x01/0x02/0x03`) — verified by disassembling `dumps/bios/700a01.22g` (crc 0x11812ef8, byte-identical to MAME's) and by MAME watchpoints on word-writes to 0x1f500000 (flash-check loop PC 0x80138b98/0x80138c1c). So values `0x01/0x02/0x03` hit `internal=0` → window returns `0xFFFF`, `array_read` (`s573_flash.v:196`) never asserts → **no SDRAM line-fill, `req` stays 0**. The upper 12 MB (banks 1-3 = chips 31l/31j/31h, program body + gfx + samples) is unreadable; the PROGRAM ROM CHECK reads all-ones and stalls/fails. |
| **Why it's #1** | Three independent witnesses (psx-spx, 573in1 `setFlashBank()`/`rom.cpp`, MAME `set_bank(m_control & 0x3f)`) all say the value IS the bank number. MAME runs **our exact data** and passes FLASH ROM CHECK for all four chips with these low-bit writes, then advances to PROGRAM ROM CHECK. Our own `tools/pack_hyperbbc.py` lays bank N at image offset N×0x400000 — so the image is packed for the low-bit decode but the RTL reads it with `[5:4]`: a **self-inconsistency**. This was a deliberate regression in commit da83148 (revert of the previously-correct `internal=(bank<4)` + `flash_word={bank[1:0],win}` decode) based on a BIOS-disasm claim that generalized from the wrong routine (`set_bank_hi`, called exactly once with value 0). |
| **Fix sketch** | `s573_flash.v:101-102` → `wire internal = (bank[5:2]==4'b0000);` and `wire [1:0] bank_idx = bank[1:0];`. This is effectively the pre-da83148 decode. Then realign the witnesses locked to the wrong encoding: `sim/tb_s573_flash.v:71-92`, `sim/tb_s573_flash_sdram.v:134-135`, `sim/tb_system573_top.v:149`, `docs/MEMORY_MAP.md:77`, and the `s573_flash.v` header comments (L7-23, L96-102, L158-159). A non-onboard/PCMCIA selector should be value ≥4 (e.g. 0x10), not 0x01. |
| **Needs hardware?** | **No** — re-run the MAME-equivalent / sim: the flash check must read banks 1/2/3 on control writes 0x01/0x02/0x03. |

### (b) Graphics garble — same root cause (FLASH-001), gated behind the stall

There is **no separate confirmed graphics-garble bug** in this audit. Garble is a *downstream consequence* of FLASH-001: banks 1-3 hold the body/graphics/sample data; with only bank 0 readable, 12 MB returns 0xFFFF → missing/corrupt tiles and sprites. But in practice the PROGRAM ROM CHECK checksum gate is hit **first** and blocks boot before any gameplay graphics render, so garble would only surface if the checksum were somehow bypassed. **Fix FLASH-001 and re-test; do not chase a phantom GPU/VRAM bug until the flash decode is corrected and the boot advances past the checksum.** No I/O-ASIC, NVRAM, ATAPI, watchdog, or DIO discrepancy in this audit affects the render path.

## 3. All confirmed discrepancies

| id | subsystem | severity | needs_hw | one-line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FLASH-001** | Flash + bank-switch | **high** | no | Bank index from `bank[5:4]` not low bits → banks 1/2/3 unreadable (0xFFFF, no fill); likely the self-test stall. `s573_flash.v:101-102` |
| **SECCART-01** | Security cart / DS2401 | **med** | no | DS2401 1-Wire line on bit 8 (I0) instead of bit 14 (I6) of 0x1f400004 → stuck-0; selftest_fail for DS2401 carts (not hyperbbc). `s573_seccart.v:60` |
| IO-001 | Konami 056879 I/O ASIC | low | no | P1/P2 buttons 4/5/6 hardwired 0 → read as permanently PRESSED (active-low idle must be 1). `s573_io.v:118,125-126` |
| IO-002 | Konami 056879 I/O ASIC | low | no | 0x0e bit10 drives TEST button instead of the RAM-layout strap (700B-only; consumer 0x1f801060 is stubbed). `s573_io.v:118,126` |
| IO-003 | Konami 056879 I/O ASIC | low | no | JAMMA P1/P2 L/R and U/D transposed, START at bit15 reads Button4 instead → start may not register. `emu.sv:1623-1624` |
| EXP1-01 | EXP1 access / byte-lane | low | no | 0x1f40000a (JVS MCU data word) undecoded → reads 0x0000; benign (JVSIRDY held 0, whole JVS channel stubbed). `s573_io.v:120-129` |
| EXP1-02 | EXP1 access / byte-lane | low | no | 0x0c and 0x0e alias same r_extra; P1/P2 extra buttons unimplemented, 0x0e bit10 mirrors test_btn. `s573_io.v:118,125-126` |
| NVRAM-01 | M48T58 NVRAM/RTC | low | no | DAY[6] battery-low bit not modeled as read-only; reset gives bit6=0 (battery-OK), benign. `m48t58.v:57,140,159` |
| NVRAM-02 | M48T58 NVRAM/RTC | low | no | Weekday increment clobbers century/century-enable bits 4-5 on midnight rollover (24h free-run needed). `m48t58.v:176` |
| ATAPI-01 | ATAPI/IDE drive | low | no | IDE reset (0x1f560000) ignores data bit0; release write (=1) re-asserts; idempotent → benign. `system573_top.v:157` |
| ATAPI-02 | ATAPI/IDE drive | low | no | CS1 page 0x4c decoded wholesale to reg index 8; alt-status only at byte 0x0c — over-broad but inert. `system573_top.v:155` |
| WDOG-02 | Watchdog 058232 | low | no | `wdog_reset` dangling at `emu.sv:1644` → watchdog bite is a no-op (≈ S86 jumper fitted). Makes WDOG-01 harmless. |
| WDOG-03 | Watchdog 058232 | low | no | 0x1f600000 EXT-OUT decoded (`sel_digout`) but never consumed; writes dropped (write-only reg, no peripheral on hyperbbc). `s573_bus.v:42` |
| WDOG-04 | Watchdog 058232 | low | no | Duplicate of ATAPI-01 (IDE reset bit0 polarity); same `system573_top.v:157`, same benign verdict. |
| DIO-01 | k573dio (Digital I/O) | low | no | 0xf6 CPLD status ID bits 14/15 swapped (returns 0xB000, HW 0x7000); hyperbbc has no DIO board. `k573dio.v:157` |
| DIO-02 | k573dio (Digital I/O) | low | no | 0xaa MP3 feed status returns 0x0000, never asserts WRDY; MP3 path is a documented stub. `k573dio.v:146-159` |

*Note: ATAPI-01 and WDOG-04 are the same defect (IDE-reset bit0 polarity at `system573_top.v:157`) filed under two subsystems; fix once.*

## 4. Refuted candidates (do not re-investigate)

- **WDOG-01** — "Watchdog timeout ~29.5 ms, ~12× too short." The numbers are correct (`watchdog.v:13` TIMEOUT_CYCLES=1_000_000 at 33.8688 MHz = 29.5 ms vs real ~350-400 ms), **but the failure mode cannot occur**: `wdog_reset` is dangling (`emu.sv:1644`) and feeds nothing (see WDOG-02), so the bite resets nothing. It is harmless dead-parameter logic. Becomes real *only if* `wdog_reset` is later wired into the core reset — in which case fix WDOG-01 **before** wiring it.
- **DIO-03** — "0x02 read returns 0x0001 with no documented register." Refuted: MAME's `k573dio.cpp` explicitly defines `map(0x02,0x03).r(a02_r)` returning exactly 0x0001 (and a00/a04/a06/a0a → 0x0000, matching our default branch). Our RTL is a byte-faithful copy of the executable reference; psx-spx's silence on 0x02 is not a positive contradiction. No divergence.

## 5. Recommended next experiments (cheapest-decisive-first)

1. **[sim, decisive] Confirm FLASH-001 is the stall.** *Hypothesis:* fixing `s573_flash.v:101-102` to the low-bit decode lets the PROGRAM ROM CHECK read banks 1-3. *Measurement:* apply the two-line change, run the existing flash sim harness driving control writes 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x03, and assert the 4 MB window returns real flash bytes (not 0xFFFF) with `array_read`/`req` asserting for each. Cross-check against MAME: the FLASH ROM CHECK passes all four chips. This is the single highest-leverage action — do it first.

2. **[trace-diff, decisive] PC-trace the post-fix boot vs MAME.** *Hypothesis:* with FLASH-001 fixed, the core advances past PROGRAM ROM CHECK to the same next stage MAME reaches. *Measurement:* run NVC boot sim + MAME 0.288 hyperbbc with PC logging; diff the trace at the flash-check dispatcher. Confirms whether a *second* gate exists beyond flash before touching hardware. (Pairs with project memory's existing dispatcher 0x8015cf88 state-3/state-5 trace work.)

3. **[sim, cheap] Regression-proof the flash decode.** *Hypothesis:* the current testbenches are blind to the bug (they assert the wrong encoding). *Measurement:* after the fix, update `sim/tb_s573_flash.v:71-92` etc. to use 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x03 for banks 0-3 and a ≥4 selector for absent/PCMCIA; verify the suite now *fails* on the old `[5:4]` decode and passes on the new one. Prevents a future da83148-style regression.

4. **[hardware, only after #1-2 pass] De-confounded warm-reboot HW capture.** *Hypothesis:* the green-0s stall clears on real HW with FLASH-001 fixed. *Measurement:* per the critical HW-test rule — warm-reboot, verify `/proc/uptime` < ~60s, exactly ONE `load_core` (avoid stale f2sdram bridge), then `frame_diff.py` each captured frame vs the green-0s ref AND vs MAME's self-test refs. **No "boots/works" claim without a frame_diff number first.** Hardware is the true arbiter but is the most expensive and confound-prone — reserve it until sim/trace are green.

5. **[low priority, batch later] Fix the latent input/accuracy cluster together** (IO-001, IO-002, IO-003, EXP1-01/02). *Hypothesis:* none affect boot, but all surface at interactive play (mirrored directions, dead START, stuck-held extra buttons). *Measurement:* once a game reaches attract/gameplay, drive one input at a time in sim (`tb_s573_io.v` with directional-semantics assertions, not the current pass-through-only check) and verify each maps to the correct r_jamma/r_extra bit. Defer until boot is solved; fix in one I/O-ASIC pass alongside the 700B multi-BIOS H8 work already TODO'd at `s573_io.v:84-85`.

6. **[deferred] SECCART-01, DIO-01/02, NVRAM-02, WDOG-03** — real but inert for hyperbbc (DS2401-bearing carts, BEMANI/DDR titles, 24h-uptime date rollover, EXT-OUT peripherals respectively). Track for multi-game/accuracy work; none gate the current target. SECCART-01 (med) is the first to fix when moving to an XI/YI/ZI cassette title: `s573_seccart.v:60` → `assign sec_in = {1'b0, ds_line, 6'b0};`.

**Methodology note (reproducible):** every verdict here is code-decidable. The objective oracle is MAME 0.288 running our actual dumps (`dumps/bios/700a01.22g` crc 0x11812ef8; `mame573/hyperbbc.zip`); the corroborating witnesses are psx-spx konamisystem573, 573in1 source, and the ST M48T58 datasheet. No discrepancy in this audit required an FPGA to *adjudicate* — hardware is needed only to *confirm the fix lands* (experiment #4).
